parts:
Bob,

In order to run stansummary I generate bat file and run from r using
system(). So this part of the message is from r system().

For some reason two chains completed successfully but the last one
silently died. So it is possible that third chain didn't form the file
correctly.

My intention was just to bring it to your attention so future releases
of stansummary are not afraid of malformed files.

On unrelated subject, I just finished the simulation of my PBPK model
successfully and would like to contribute the model as a stan success
story (assumed it adds value to community). The model is similar to the
one in Gelman Bois paper but is about drug and much larger. Both blood
concentration for 19 subjects and urine were fitted. I have supplied
jacobian - it takes 24 hours to get 1200 draws (200 warmup). It has 10
parameters and 8 random effects. I had to use truncation since one
parameter had multiple modes. And the model was a very stiff system of
ODEs. If if adds value please guide me in the contribution process.

I still thank some improvements can be done - like cholesky.

With regards to truncation. I wanted all 10 parameters to be called
theta so I put lower bound on the array theta. I have found that
theta[6] had to be truncated - so I put truncation on the prior. If
truncation doesn't cause convergence/speed/etc problems I would like to
leave as is since it is more understandable - at least for me.

After I added one more parameter and corresponding random effect the
convergence pace became similar.

The final code is below.

Linas

data {
int <lower = 1> T; // number of unique time points
int <lower = 1> N; // number of states
int <lower = 1> Nparam; // number of parameters to estimate
int <lower = 1> Nobs; // number of observations
int <lower = 1> N_IND; // number of individuals
int <lower = 1> N_grp1; // number of individuals in group 1
int <lower = 1, upper = N> idx; // index of state to predict
int <lower = 1, upper = N_IND> ind_idx [Nobs];
// individual for each observation
int <lower = 1, upper = T> ts_idx [Nobs];
// time index for each observation
vector <lower = 0, upper = 1> [N_IND] group_idx;
// group index for each individual
int <lower = 0, upper = N_IND> grp1_idx [N_IND];
// index for individual in group 1
real <lower = 0> y0 [N]; // initial concentrations
real <lower = 0> t0; // initial time
real <lower = 0> uts [T]; // unique time points
vector <lower = 0> [Nobs] y; // observations
vector <lower = 0> [N_IND] urine; // urine observations
int <lower = 1, upper = N> idx_urine; // index of metKidney
}
transformed data {
int x_i [0];
real x_r [0];
vector [N_IND] lurine;
vector [N_IND] one;
vector [Nobs] ly;
int n_raneff;

lurine = log (urine);
one = to_vector (rep_array (1., N_IND));
ly = log (y);
n_raneff = 7;
}
parameters {
real <lower = 0> sigma_prop;
real <lower = 0> theta [Nparam];
real <lower = 0> sigma_urine;
matrix [n_raneff, N_IND] u;
vector [N_grp1] uu;
vector <lower = 0> [n_raneff] sigma_ind;
real <lower = 0> sigma_ind_kid;
}
transformed parameters {
real y_hat_ind [N_IND, T, N];
real <lower = 0> theta_ind [N_IND, Nparam];
vector [Nobs] ly_p;

// random effect: log(theta_ind)~N(log(theta),sigma_ind)
theta_ind [, 1] = to_array_1d (theta [1] * exp (u [3] * sigma_ind
[3])); // kpu_scale
for (i in 1 : N_IND) {
if (group_idx [i] == 0)
theta_ind [i, 2] = theta [2] * theta [3] * exp (uu [grp1_idx
[i]] * sigma_ind_kid);
// kid_vmax, random effect, group 1
else
theta_ind [i, 2] = 0; // kid_vmax=0, group 2
}
theta_ind [, 3] = to_array_1d (theta [3] * one); // kid_km
theta_ind [, 4] = to_array_1d (theta [4] * theta [5] * theta [7] * exp
(u [7] * sigma_ind [7])); // acat_vmax_duo
theta_ind [, 5] = to_array_1d (theta [5] * theta [7] * exp (u [2] *
sigma_ind [2])); // acat_vmax_jej
theta_ind [, 6] = to_array_1d (theta [6] * theta [5] * theta [7] * exp
(u [5] * sigma_ind [5])); // acat_vmax_ill
theta_ind [, 7] = to_array_1d (theta [7] * one); // acat_km
theta_ind [, 8] = to_array_1d (theta [8] * exp (u [4] * sigma_ind
[4])); // CL_glom
theta_ind [, 9] = to_array_1d (theta [9] * exp (u [1] * sigma_ind
[1])); // k_leave_1, random effect
theta_ind [, 10] = to_array_1d (theta [9] * exp (u [6] * sigma_ind
[6])); // k_leave_2, random effect
for (i in 1 : N_IND)
y_hat_ind [i] = integrate_ode_bdf (pbpk, y0, t0, uts, theta_ind
[i], x_r, x_i);
for (n in 1 : Nobs)
ly_p [n] = log (y_hat_ind [ind_idx [n], ts_idx [n], idx]);
}
model {
sigma_prop ~ normal (0.37, 0.1);
theta [1] ~ lognormal (-0.4, 0.1); // kpu_scale
theta [2] ~ lognormal (-0.6, 0.4); // kid_vmax/kid_km
theta [3] ~ lognormal (6.23, 2.2); // kid_km
theta [4] ~ lognormal (-7.1, 1.1); // acat_vmax_duo/acat_vmax_jej
theta [5] ~ lognormal (-0.37, 0.1); // acat_vmax_jej/acat_km
theta [6] ~ lognormal (-4.5, 0.9) T [, 1]; //
acat_vmax_ill/acat_vmax_jej
theta [7] ~ lognormal (12.21, 1); // acat_km
theta [8] ~ lognormal (1.8, 0.1); // CL_glom
theta [9] ~ lognormal (0.68, 0.1); // k_leave_1
theta [10] ~ lognormal (0.81, 0.3); // k_leave_2
to_vector (u) ~ normal (0, 1);
uu ~ normal (0, 1);
sigma_ind [1] ~ normal (0.52, 0.4); // k_leave_1
sigma_ind [2] ~ normal (0.08, 0.2); // acat_vmax_jej
sigma_ind [3] ~ normal (0.12, 0.2); // kpu_scale
sigma_ind [4] ~ normal (0.12, 0.1); // CL_glom
sigma_ind [5] ~ normal (0.99, 1.8); // acat_vmax_ill
sigma_ind [6] ~ normal (0.44, 0.5); // k_leave_2
sigma_ind [7] ~ normal (0.7, 1); // acat_vmax_duo
sigma_ind_kid ~ normal (0.43, 1); // acat_vmax_duo
ly ~ normal (ly_p, sigma_prop);
sigma_urine ~ normal (0.26, 0.1); // exp err model
lurine ~ normal (log (to_vector (y_hat_ind [, T, idx_urine])),
sigma_urine); // exp err model
// sigma_urine ~ normal (0, 200); // add err model
// urine ~ normal (to_vector (y_hat_ind [, T, idx_urine]),
sigma_urine); // prop err model
}

Thanks. We should be capturing ill-formed files and
throwing Stan exceptions, and that may be what's happening
before the other pieces of the puzzle get in between. You'd
have to run directly from CmdStan to see what the output from
Stan itself was.

> On unrelated subject, I just finished the simulation of my PBPK model successfully and would like to contribute the model as a stan success story (assumed it adds value to community). The model is similar to the one in Gelman Bois paper but is about drug and much larger. Both blood concentration for 19 subjects and urine were fitted. I have supplied jacobian - it takes 24 hours to get 1200 draws (200 warmup). It has 10 parameters and 8 random effects. I had to use truncation since one parameter had multiple modes. And the model was a very stiff system of ODEs. If if adds value please guide me in the contribution process.
>
> I still thank some improvements can be done - like cholesky.
>
> With regards to truncation. I wanted all 10 parameters to be called theta so I put lower bound on the array theta. I have found that theta[6] had to be truncated - so I put truncation on the prior. If truncation doesn't cause convergence/speed/etc problems I would like to leave as is since it is more understandable - at least for me.

It can work if you get lucky or control initialization and there isn't any
probability mass near the boundary that you're not properly constraining.

We generally recommend making sure that any parameter values that
satisfy the declared constraints have a positive density (finite
log density).

Understandability is very much in the eye of the beholder. The issue
I have with the way you're doing it is that there are unwritten constraints
that aren't apparent from looking at the model itself, at least not without
linking a bunch of the pieces. That is, you're not treating theta homogeneously
in the model, but you're declaring it as a homogeneously constrained parameter.

- Bob
